overview.title: Project overview
overview.content: At Knowledgehook, I was responsible for optimizing and scaling our in-house design system, which had become fragmented and inefficient. Although a system existed, it lacked structure and consistency, making it difficult for design and development teams to work effectively. My goal was to transform it into a unified, scalable foundation that improved collaboration, efficiency, and product quality across teams.

intro.title: Role
content: UI designer

intro.title: Team
content: Leah - Design, Rita - Product Lead, Lambo -Dev Lead

intro.title: Timeline
content: Jan 2022 - Jan 2024

intro.title: Tools
content: Figma, Zeroheight, Microsoft Azure

discovery.title: 🔍Identifying Structural Limitations
discovery.content: During the discovery phase, I conducted an in-depth audit of the token system and component library. While the existing structure provided a foundational setup, it was not designed with scalability or future growth in mind. As a result, the system lacked the flexibility needed to support evolving product requirements, leading to inconsistencies and inefficiencies across teams.

problem.title: Inconsistent Token Structure
content: Token naming and usage lack consistency, and primitive tokens are not scalable.
Lack of details of color usage and style guide.

problem.title: Missing Responsive Framework
content: Text tokens don’t support responsive design.
Lack of layout elements such as grid style, breakpoints.

problem.title: Styles Not Fully Tokenized
content: Certain styles (e.g., box-shadow) are hardcoded instead of defined as tokens, leading to inconsistency.

problem.title: Incomplete Component System
content: Lack of systematic design guideline and documentation for designers and developers to use and build components.
Communication gaps cause misalignment between designers and developers during implementation.
Some components are not pass the WCAG.

approach.title: 📑Research - Learning from Industry Best Practices
approach.content: To guide the restructuring process, I studied leading design systems—particularly Material Design and Carbon Design System—which shared similar technical foundations. This research provided valuable insights into scalable structures and best practices that informed our system improvements.

solutionA.sub: Solutions for building consistency and accessibility
solutionA.title: 🟣All start from a token.
content: In our case, we had an existing system, but over time, it had grown messy—with overlapping styles, non-standard tokens, and accessibility gaps that made it hard to maintain or trust.
I took a ground-up approach to audit, clean, and rebuild the system, ensuring it would support both visual consistency and inclusive design.

breakdowns.heading: 🧱1. Rebuilding the Token Architecture: A Cleaner Foundation
breakdowns.content: It all started with the tokens. I conducted a full audit of the existing token sheet, which had bundled things like CSS overrides and even brand assets like logos into the same system—creating confusion for both designers and developers. To fix this, I:
list: Removed non-token elements (e.g., CSS, logos) from the sheet
Standardized the structure to include only token name, value, and usage
Made tokens easier to reference and apply consistently in design tools and codebases

breakdowns.heading: 🧩 2. Introducing Component-Specific Token Naming
breakdowns.content: To push consistency even further, I introduced a component-based naming convention for tokens.Instead of relying on vague or global names, tokens now clearly map to their purpose within a specific UI element (e.g., $button-primary-bg vs $color-blue-500).This approach helped:
list: Designers quickly identify and apply the right tokens
Developers implement UI with cleaner, more maintainable code
Reduce styling inconsistencies across components and teams

breakdowns.heading: ♿3. Embedding Accessibility through Testing & Standards
breakdowns.content: To ensure our system met accessibility guidelines, I ran a series of color accessibility tests across text, icons, and component backgrounds using WCAG 2.2 standards.This included:
list: Verifying contrast ratios for text and icons across all themes
Making adjustments to brand colors and states (e.g., hover, disabled) where necessary
Documenting accessible use cases and providing design guidance in our system documentation

solutionB.title: 📱Optimizing Responsiveness Across Devices
content: As our products grew, we faced inconsistent experiences across screen sizes due to a lack of responsive structure. To solve this, I leveraged both my design and front-end knowledge to integrate a responsive foundation directly into the design system—ensuring our UI could adapt fluidly across devices.

breakdowns.heading: 🔠 1. Responsive Text Sizing
breakdowns.content: I introduced CSS clamp() for fluid, viewport-based text sizing—enhancing readability across devices without sacrificing hierarchy. These responsive tokens were integrated into Figma styles and documentation, enabling designers to apply them confidently and consistently.

breakdowns.heading: 📐 2. Flexible Breakpoints & Grid System
breakdowns.content: I standardized a set of responsive breakpoints and defined a flexible grid system that worked seamlessly across layouts. These were built into both our component templates and documentation, enabling:
list: Design flexibility for different screen widths
Cleaner handoffs with well-defined layout rules
Faster prototyping of responsive UI in Figma

solutionC.title: 👩‍💻Making the Design System Truly Useful for Designers & Developers
content: To make the design system truly useful, it had to be adopted and understood—not just built. I gathered feedback from designers and developers to understand their needs, then partnered with two developers to co-create a scalable, collaborative system. Here's how we made it happen:

breakdowns.heading: 📘 1. Building Shared Component Documentation
content: I created and maintained a comprehensive documentation hub using Figma, Zeroheight, and Azure, covering:
list: Visual design guides and usage patterns
Do’s and Don’ts to support best practices

breakdowns.heading: 🧮2. Implementing Tokens & Variables for Design-Code Alignment
content: I standardized a set of responsive breakpoints and defined a flexible grid system that worked seamlessly across layouts. These were built into both our component templates and documentation, enabling:
This not only made the UI more consistent and easier to maintain, but it also bridged the gap between design and development—ensuring that values in Figma matched what developers implemented in code.

breakdowns.heading: 🤝 3. Creating a Feedback Loop with Regular Syncs
content: To foster continuous collaboration, I:
list: Shared system updates regularly on Zeroheight and our team Slack channels
Led monthly design system syncs with designers and developers to review updates, resolve issues, and align on priorities

impact.sub: Impact of the Optimized Design System
impact.title: How does it work?

impactBreakdowns.heading: 🎨 Consistency and Design Speed
details: We developed a systematic component library and comprehensive documentation that significantly improved both design consistency and workflow efficiency. As a result, we reduced the average design and hand-off time by 50%, while improving visual and interaction consistency by 80% across products.
The scalable nature of the system also allowed us to introduce multiple design themes, enabling greater flexibility—currently supporting two distinct themes to cater to different product needs.

impactBreakdowns.heading: 💻 Design to Dev Workflow
details: By implementing a robust token system and clear documentation, we established a shared language between designers and developers, strengthening cross-functional collaboration.
The use of reusable, standardized components helped the engineering team reduce redundant work and significantly cut down development time for new features and UI updates.

impactBreakdowns.heading: 🧑 User Feedback
details: The new design system enabled faster and more cohesive UI revamps. With a cleaner, more intuitive interface, we received positive feedback from both teachers and student users, who noted improvements in usability and visual clarity.
Overall, users reported feeling more engaged and satisfied, thanks to a more consistent, responsive, and accessible experience across the platform.
